description:
We are VANGUARD POLARIS, a two-member team interested in science, programming, technology, and space exploration. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are working on ASTRA HEALTH, a project focused on monitoring astronaut health during long-duration space missions.

We would be happy to work with people interested in coding, software development, data science, AI, design, medicine, or space science. We value curiosity, teamwork, and practical ideas.
summary:
ASTRA HEALTH is an explainable astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed to help organize and understand health information during space missions. It provides an interactive dashboard where users can explore body systems, enter health observations, review symptom reports, and track changes through visual charts and illustrative alerts.

The project aims to make complex health information easier to review by presenting observations in a clear, structured, and understandable way. Its rule-based monitoring approach demonstrates how health data could be organized to support astronaut well-being and mission awareness.

ASTRA HEALTH was developed as a local software prototype using Python and Streamlit, with data visualization and local data storage features. It is an early-stage concept and is not a medical device or a substitute for professional medical assessment.
details:
ASTRA HEALTH is an interactive software prototype developed to explore how astronaut health information could be organized and reviewed during space missions.

The application includes a Mission Dashboard, an Interactive Body Map, Health Input forms, Symptom Reports, Mission Intelligence charts, a Mission Review Queue, JSON data export, and a Space Health Knowledge Base. Users can enter health observations, explore body systems, review reported symptoms, and follow changes over time through visual summaries.

The prototype uses a transparent, rule-based approach to generate illustrative alerts. This makes the reasoning behind each alert easier to understand instead of presenting unexplained predictions. The application stores its information locally using SQLite and provides a structured interface for reviewing mission-related health observations.

The project was built with Python and Streamlit, using Plotly for interactive visualizations and Pandas for data handling. SQLite is used for local storage.

Our main design considerations were clarity, explainability, accessibility of information, and the special challenges of monitoring health during space missions. We wanted to demonstrate how a structured digital tool could help make complex information easier to interpret.

ASTRA HEALTH is an early-stage educational and research prototype. It does not connect to live astronaut sensors or telemetry, does not use a trained machine-learning model, and has not been clinically or operationally validated. Its illustrative alerts are not medical diagnoses or flight decisions.
